description: We're a team that blends game development with web and software development. We combine systems logic with interactive mechanics to create games that challenge players to make critical decisions. You should join us if you're looking for a team with a strong technical foundation and a deep passion for coding. We're currently seeking creative talent in UI/UX design, 2D art, illustration, and technical storytelling.
summary:
More Resources, Please! is an interactive space mission design simulator developed in the Godot 4 engine. The project tackles the space mission design challenge by allowing players to manage complex engineering constraints, such as strict budgets, spacecraft mass limits, precise Delta-V margins, power generation, and scientific instrument selection.

This proposal directly addresses the challenge by transforming orbital mechanics and resource limitations into strategic, high-stakes decision-making scenarios across multiple missions, complemented by agency director negotiations, launch audits, and real-time telemetry.

Its importance lies in building a unique bridge between aerospace education and interactive experience design, providing students and enthusiasts with a practical understanding of the rigorous technical and economic decisions that define the success of real space exploration.
details:
1. What does it do, and how does it work?

"More Resources, Please!" is an interactive space mission simulator inspired by the tense, decision-driven mechanics.

Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge by team "Ping 1ms 'I Gotta Believe'", the game puts players in the shoes of a lead aerospace systems engineer working under strict agency oversight.

  • The Workflow: Each mission begins with a dossier from Director Elena Vance outlining base parameters (budget, mass limits, Delta-V, and science requirements). Players then meet with scientific clients at the window, negotiate contract clauses, and head into the hangar.
  • Subsystem Assembly & Launch Audit: In the hangar, players configure and balance critical spacecraft modules across categories like power generation (solar vs. RTG), propulsion, avionics, EDL (Entry, Descent, and Landing), and scientific instruments.
  • Destination Telemetry & Outcomes: Before launch, the game runs a rigorous structural audit. Once airborne, players face real-time destination telemetry events (such as lunar eclipses, atmospheric entry hazards, or Jovian radiation belts) where choosing the correct maneuver dictates mission success or a disciplinary citation.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Educational Accessibility: It bridges the gap between complex aerospace engineering and interactive entertainment, making orbital mechanics, mass budgeting, and power constraints intuitive.
  • Critical Thinking Development: It teaches players how to weigh competing priorities, such as balancing high-reward scientific payloads against strict mass and budget ceilings.
  • Replayability & Depth: With multiple mission tiers (ranging from LEO climate observation to deep space interstellar probes) and branching narrative choices, it offers varied strategic playthroughs.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

The intended impact is to inspire and educate students and space enthusiasts by demystifying how real-world space missions are planned and executed.

By experiencing firsthand the tight margins and high-stakes trade-offs that real aerospace engineers face, players gain a deeper appreciation for systems thinking, scientific rigor, and the economic realities of space exploration.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Game Engine & Language: Built entirely using Godot 4 Engine and written in GDScript for clean, modular object-oriented logic and UI management.
  • Version Control & Collaboration: Managed collaboratively via GitHub repositories (MoreResourcesPlease) to coordinate code, scripts, and scene trees between team members.
  • Development Hardware & Software: Developed on a custom Windows desktop rig featuring an AMD Ryzen 7 5700 processor, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti graphics card, and Patriot Viper Steel 16GB DDR4 RAM, 2 Crua Monitors, 2 Lenovo Laptops, using Visual Studio Code, Godot Editor, Gemini for SI, PowerPoint, Excel, Krita, Google Chrome, WhatsApp, Affinity.

5. How is your project creative?

The project's creativity lies in its unique genre fusion.

Instead of a traditional sandbox or arcade space game, it treats space exploration through a bureaucratic, high-stakes engineering lens, when the tension comes not from twitch reflexes, but from reading technical specifications, managing finite funds, handling demanding institutional stakeholders (like Director Elena Vance or specialized research directors), and surviving strict launch audits where a single overlooked kilogram or watt means mission failure.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  • Real-World Engineering Veracity: Balancing game fun with realistic physics principles, such as inverse-square solar irradiance drop-offs at Jupiter, radiation vault requirements, and Delta-V mass ratios.
  • User Experience & UI Design: Structuring the interface to avoid text overflow or cramped menus, ensuring that stats (budget, mass, science, power) remain visible and responsive.
  • Bilingual Localization: Implementing a robust translation framework supporting both English and Spanish, to ensure accessibility for a wider international audience.
  • Progressive Difficulty Curve: Designing a smooth learning curve that transitions players from basic low-Earth orbit satellites (Tier 1) to complex deep-space frontier architectures (Tier 6) with zero margin for error.
